senses.gloss:
jalakṛcchra
(‘penance in or with water’)
------------------------------------------
Expiation for sins committed, knowingly or unknowingly, by performing the prescribed penances is an ancient practice in हिन्दुइस्म्. ‘Kṛcchra’ is a general term applied to many of these expiations. Jalakṛcchra—also called toyakṛcchra, udakakṛcchra or varuṇakṛcchra—is one of them.
It has been described in several ways. According to one version, it consists in subsisting only on water mixed with ground barley, for one month.
Another version is that the sinner should spend a whole day and night ड़स्तिन्ग्, and immersing himself in water. This should be followed by the repetition of the Gāyatrīmantra 1008 times the next day.
See also KṚCCHRA.

jalpa
------------------------------------------
Indian philosophical systems generally adopt a twofold method in propagating their teachings: statement of their principles and countering the arguments of the opponents. Among the various methods of the latter, जल्प is also one. In this type, each of the disputants tries to demolish the arguments of the opponent and establish his own standpoint or theory or principle using appropriate means of knowledge. In this method, the desire to win is stronger than the desire to know the truth!
See also VĀDA and VITAṆḌĀ.

jālandharabandha
------------------------------------------
Works on हठयोग concentrate on various exercises known as āsanas and mudrās or bandhas by which the longevity, health and stamina of the body can be increased.
The जालन्धरबन्ध is one such exercise wherein the throat has to be contracted and the chin pressed firmly against the chest.
It is capable of destroying a number of diseases of the throat.
More details—many of which quite complicated—are given in the treatises like the Haṭhayogapradīpikā, the Dhyāna-बिन्दु Upaniṣad, the Yogaśikhā Upaniṣad and others. However the exercises have to be practised under the direct care of experts.
